```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(pdmS7)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  error = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 3.8, dpi = if (nzchar(Sys.getenv("IN_PKGDOWN"))) 110 else 60
)
logger::log_threshold(logger::WARN, namespace = "pdmS7")
pal <- c(dark = "#444444", blue = "#236b83", orange = "#a26421", green = "#5b8c3a",
         grey = "#9aa7b0")
f2 <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)
f3 <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f", x)
```

Some rivers answer rain twice. A sharp spike comes within an hour or two and is gone within a
few more; a slower flood hydrograph follows and recedes over a day or two; baseflow carries on
for weeks. The spike comes from ground that sheds water at once: roads and roofs, saturated
ground by the channel, thin soils on steep slopes. The rest comes from the soils of the
catchment at large.

One PDM has two routes to the outlet, a fast surface route and a slow groundwater route. Asked
to make three timescales with two, a calibration bends one of them to do two jobs, and the
parameters show it. This article describes the two-zone PDM in pdmS7, which adds a third
timescale in the way the published model allows, and shows it at work on a made-up catchment
whose truth is known.

# The signs that one zone is not enough

On a real flashy catchment, a single-zone calibration tends to show three things together:

- **Parameters pinned at their limits.** A split recharge share `recharge.alpha` at its lower
  bound (nearly all runoff sent to groundwater), with the groundwater store doing the flood
  routing; or surface stores at the slowest values allowed. The search is pressing against the
  fences in every fit, whatever the structure.
- **An events stage that wants something else.** Fitted to the largest floods alone, the
  surface stores go very fast, an hour or less, and the overall fit falls apart, because the
  same stores must also carry the slow flood hydrograph.
- **Peaks too low and too late** on the largest floods, however the stores are set.

Fences and caps on one zone cannot fix this: it is a missing timescale, not a wrong value.

# The model

The PDM for PCs configuration guide (section 5) allows several hydrological zones: complete
PDMs over parts of the catchment, each with its own parameters, area and delay, whose flows
add at the outlet. pdmS7's two-zone PDM keeps the catchment's usual PDM as the **main zone**
and adds a small **fast zone** that does one job only: the spike.

```{r diagram, echo=FALSE, fig.height=3.2, fig.cap="The two-zone PDM. Both zones read the same rain and evaporation; their flows add at the outlet. The fast zone has no groundwater path."}
par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
box_at <- function(x, y, label, col = pal[["blue"]], w = 0.17, h = 0.13) {
  rect(x - w / 2, y - h / 2, x + w / 2, y + h / 2, col = adjustcolor(col, 0.15), border = col)
  text(x, y, label, cex = 0.8)
}
arrow <- function(x0, y0, x1, y1) arrows(x0, y0, x1, y1, length = 0.07, col = pal[["dark"]])
box_at(0.5, 0.92, "Rain and evaporation (the same depths for both zones)", col = pal[["dark"]],
       w = 0.6, h = 0.1)
box_at(0.25, 0.65, "Main zone\nsoil store")
box_at(0.12, 0.35, "Surface\ncascade")
box_at(0.38, 0.35, "Groundwater\nstore")
box_at(0.75, 0.65, "Fast zone\nsmall soil store", col = pal[["orange"]])
box_at(0.75, 0.35, "One linear\nstore, ~1 h", col = pal[["orange"]])
box_at(0.5, 0.08, "Outlet: flows added", col = pal[["green"]], w = 0.3, h = 0.1)
arrow(0.3, 0.87, 0.27, 0.72); arrow(0.7, 0.87, 0.73, 0.72)
arrow(0.2, 0.58, 0.14, 0.42); arrow(0.3, 0.58, 0.36, 0.42); arrow(0.75, 0.58, 0.75, 0.42)
arrow(0.14, 0.28, 0.42, 0.13); arrow(0.38, 0.28, 0.46, 0.13); arrow(0.75, 0.28, 0.58, 0.13)
text(0.27, 0.79, "share 1 - s", cex = 0.75, col = pal[["blue"]], pos = 2)
text(0.73, 0.79, "share s", cex = 0.75, col = pal[["orange"]], pos = 4)
```

The fast zone is a complete PDM, so every parameter has a value, but most are locked. Four
are searched:

| Parameter | Starting value | Searched |
|---|---|---|
| Share of the catchment area, `zones.fast.share` | 0.1 | 0.01 to 0.3 |
| Soil store: Pareto, `cmax` | 20 mm (with `b` 0.5) | `cmax`, 1 to 100 mm |
| Recharge: split, `alpha` 1 | all direct runoff to the surface, none to groundwater | no |
| Surface: one linear store, `kb` | 1 h | 0.25 to 12 h |
| Groundwater: linear, `kb` 1000 h | never fed | no |
| Delay, `td` | 0 h | 0 to 6 h |
| Evaporation exponent `be` | the main zone's | no |

The fast zone can only make quick runoff: its recharge sends nothing to groundwater. So it
cannot trade baseflow with the main zone, and the two zones keep their roles. That is what
makes the extra four parameters identifiable from a flow record: a second full PDM, with its
own groundwater, would add seven and could swap water with the main zone without explaining
anything new.

# The rain adds up

Both zones read the same rain and evaporation depths, the catchment average, in mm per step.
A zone's rain volume is that depth over its own area, and the two areas add up to the
catchment's, so the rain volume over the zones is exactly the catchment's. The rainfall factor
`fc` is set once, for both zones: locked at 1 by default, and if it is unlocked, it scales the
rain on both zones together. Each zone's water balance closes on its own; the outlet flow is the
sum of the zones' flows, and depth columns such as `soil_mm` and the balance are area-weighted.

```{r adds-up}
cfg <- pdm_presets("standard")
cfg$area_km2 <- 30
two <- two_zone_config(cfg, share = 0.12)
model <- pdm_from_config(two)
vapply(model@zones, function(z) c(area_km2 = z@area_km2, fc = z@fc), numeric(2))
```

# A made-up flashy catchment

The true catchment here is a two-zone PDM: 12 per cent of it sheds rain through a store of
0.6 hours; the rest is a standard PDM. Rain falls in bursts over eight months of hourly data,
and the gauge adds 3 per cent noise.

```{r truth}
set.seed(5)
n <- 24 * 240
time <- as.POSIXct("2020-10-01", tz = "UTC") + 3600 * (seq_len(n) - 1)
forcing <- data.frame(time = time, pet = 0.07,
                      rain = ifelse(stats::runif(n) < 0.07, stats::rexp(n, 0.25), 0))
truth <- two
truth$zones$fast$surface$kb <- 0.6
truth$zones$fast$distribution$cmax <- 8
truth_model <- pdm_from_config(truth)
start <- initial_state_from_flow(truth_model, 0.5, 0.7)
observed <- run_pdm(truth_model, forcing, start)$output$q_m3s * exp(stats::rnorm(n, 0, 0.03))
```

The hydrograph of a storm shows the two zones' parts: the fast zone's spike on top of the main
zone's slower response.

```{r parts, fig.cap="One storm in the made-up catchment: the observed flow, and the true model's two zones, stacked."}
zones <- lapply(names(truth_model@zones), function(z) {
  run_pdm(truth_model@zones[[z]], forcing, start@states[[z]])$output$q_m3s
})
peak <- which.max(observed[seq_len(n / 2)])
shown <- (peak - 18):(peak + 60)
par(mar = c(2.5, 4.2, 0.6, 0.6))
plot(time[shown], observed[shown], type = "n", xlab = "", ylab = "Flow (m3/s)", las = 1,
     ylim = c(0, max(observed[shown])))
polygon(c(time[shown], rev(time[shown])), c(zones[[1]][shown], rep(0, length(shown))),
        col = adjustcolor(pal[["blue"]], 0.25), border = NA)
polygon(c(time[shown], rev(time[shown])), c(zones[[1]][shown] + zones[[2]][shown],
                                             rev(zones[[1]][shown])),
        col = adjustcolor(pal[["orange"]], 0.35), border = NA)
lines(time[shown], observed[shown], col = pal[["dark"]])
legend("topright", c("observed", "main zone", "fast zone"), bty = "n", cex = 0.8,
       lwd = c(1, 8, 8), col = c(pal[["dark"]], adjustcolor(pal[["blue"]], 0.25),
                                 adjustcolor(pal[["orange"]], 0.35)))
```

# One zone against two

Each structure is calibrated alike: every parameter in `calibration_bounds()`, by DDS, on the
first five months, from a steady start at the first observed flow.

```{r fits}
calibration <- seq_len(24 * 150)
fit_one <- function(config) {
  b <- calibration_bounds(config)
  calibrate_pdm(config, forcing[calibration, ], observed[calibration],
                lower = stats::setNames(b$lower, b$path), upper = stats::setNames(b$upper, b$path),
                log_scale = b$path[b$scale == "log"], warmup = 24 * 14, method = "dds",
                starts = 2, seed = 1, control = list(maxit = 400))
}
one <- suppressWarnings(fit_one(cfg))
both <- suppressWarnings(fit_one(two))
round(both$parameters[grepl("fast", names(both$parameters))], 3)
```

```{r compare}
cmp <- compare_calibrations(
  list(one_zone = one$config, two_zones = both$config), forcing, observed,
  windows = list(calibration = c("2020-10-15", "2021-02-27"),
                 validation = c("2021-02-28", "2021-05-28")),
  markers = c("Q1", "Q5")
)
cmp$scores[cmp$scores$score %in% c("nse", "log_nse"), ]
```

```{r compare-numbers, include=FALSE}
nse <- function(m, w) cmp$scores[[m]][cmp$scores$window == w & cmp$scores$score == "nse"]
fast <- both$parameters
peak_err <- function(m) stats::median(abs(cmp$events[[paste0(m, ".peak_error")]]), na.rm = TRUE)
```

The two-zone fit puts `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * fast[["zones.fast.share"]])` per cent of the
area in the fast zone, against a true 12, with a store of `r f2(fast[["zones.fast.surface.kb"]])`
hours against a true 0.6; its soil store, at `r sprintf("%.0f", fast[["zones.fast.distribution.cmax"]])` mm against a true 8, is the least certain of the four. On the validation months, which neither fit saw, its NSE is
`r f3(nse("two_zones", "validation"))` against `r f3(nse("one_zone", "validation"))` for one
zone, and its median peak error on the largest floods
`r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * peak_err("two_zones"))` per cent against
`r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * peak_err("one_zone"))`.

```{r flood, fig.cap="The largest flood of the record: observed flow, the one-zone fit and the two-zone fit."}
plot(cmp)
```

# In a calibration project

`calibrate_project()` decides between one zone and two as the last step of the structure
recommendation, with `zones = c(1, 2)`:

```{r project, eval=FALSE}
calibrate_project(project, forcing, observed, area_km2 = 36.7,
                  calibration = c("2010-10-01", "2019-09-30"),
                  validation = c("2019-10-01", "2025-06-30"),
                  recommend = TRUE, zones = c(1, 2), report = TRUE)
```

The recharge rule, soil store and groundwater store are chosen first, as one zone. The last
step then calibrates that structure as one zone and with a fast zone added, and keeps two only
if they score better on the validation window by more than the tie tolerance (0.02 in NSE)
and no parameter is pinned at a bound; otherwise one zone stays. The choice and its reason are
written to the log, and the staged calibration then runs on whichever won: the water balance
of both zones first, then the fast responses with the fast zone's share and delay, then a
polish over everything, then the events stage. `zones = 2` uses two zones without the
comparison; the default, `zones = 1`, keeps one.

Bounds you give for the single-zone model carry over: an override or exclusion without a
`zones.` prefix, such as `surface.k1 = c(0.5, 12)`, applies to the main zone.

# Reading the result

A two-zone calibration that has found a real spike looks like this:

- **A small fast zone.** A share of a few per cent to a fifth, and a store time constant of
  about an hour. A share pressed against 0.3, or a store of many hours, means the fast zone is
  doing the main zone's work, and the second zone is not earning its place.
- **The main zone freed.** Its split recharge share and surface stores come off their limits,
  because it no longer has to make the spike.
- **Better floods on validation,** in peak size and timing, not only a better NSE.

If none of these holds, the extra zone is fitting noise, and one zone with judgement is the
better model.

# What it is not

- **Not a map of the catchment.** The fast zone's share is fitted from the flow record, not
  measured from land cover. It may match the urban or near-channel area, and that is worth
  checking, but it is a calibrated parameter.
- **Not for every catchment.** On most rivers one PDM is enough, and the extra parameters cost
  identifiability. Let the structure step decide, and prefer one zone when it does not
  clearly win.
- **Single-zone tools stay single-zone.** Forecast updating, hindcasts, the events workbench in
  the app and PDM for PCs input files are for one zone. A two-zone candidate is simulated,
  calibrated, scored, compared and reported like any other.

Moore, R.J. (2007). The PDM rainfall-runoff model. *Hydrology and Earth System Sciences*,
11(1), 483-499. doi:10.5194/hess-11-483-2007.
